_readme: Per-snippet settings for scripts/runSnippets.js. Snippets are discovered from
snippets/ automatically -- a new .py/.ts/.js/.go file runs with the defaults
(mode 'exit', 120s, no credentials) without being listed here. Add an entry
only to change that.
Keys:
mode            'exit' (must exit 0 before the timeout) or 'long-running'
(a worker loop with no natural end -- still alive at the
timeout is a pass, exiting non-zero is a failure).
timeoutSeconds  How long the snippet gets.
requires        Credentials the snippet needs: 'apiKey' -> ALLORA_API_KEY,
'wallet' -> ALLORA_WALLET_MNEMONIC. The runner refuses to
start if a required variable is unset, and writes the
mnemonic to .allora_key in the run directory so the worker
never prompts on a CI runner's absent stdin.
pip / npm       Extra packages for the clean toolchain.
files           Sibling snippets to copy in under a different name, for
snippets that import a companion module.
skip / reason   Opt a file out of execution. A reason is mandatory in
review: an unexplained skip is a silent coverage hole.
An entry naming a file that no longer exists is a hard error, so exclusions
cannot outlive the snippet they were written for.
'toolchain' is what the pages tell readers to install, and nothing else --
if a snippet needs a package that is not listed here or in its own 'pip'/
'npm', the page is missing an install step.

worker_model.py.reason: trains on candles from a third-party market-data API (api.binance.com) whose availability depends on the runner's egress region; a block there would be reported as a docs failure it is not. Run it locally: python model.py.

worker_with_model.py.reason: imports worker_model.py, so it inherits the same third-party market-data dependency. Unskip both together once the runner's egress is known to reach that API.
